content: This updated review evaluates the effectiveness of single-dose oral ibuprofen for managing acute postoperative pain in adults. Ibuprofen, a widely used non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID), is commonly prescribed or purchased over-the-counter for both acute and chronic pain conditions. The objective of this review was to assess the analgesic efficacy of single oral doses of ibuprofen in adults experiencing moderate to severe postoperative pain. The review included randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials that investigated single-dose oral ibuprofen in adults with acute postoperative pain. Pain relief or intensity data were analyzed, focusing on the proportion of participants achieving at least 50% pain relief over a 4 to 6-hour period. Additional measures of efficacy included the use of rescue medication and the time to its use. Adverse events and participant withdrawals were also documented. A total of 72 studies involving 9186 participants compared ibuprofen to placebo. The majority of the data focused on ibuprofen doses of 200 mg and 400 mg. For achieving at least 50% pain relief, the number needed to treat (NNT) was 2.7 (95% CI: 2.5 to 3.0) for 200 mg and 2.5 (95% CI: 2.4 to 2.6) for 400 mg. The proportion of participants achieving at least 50% pain relief was 46% with 200 mg and 54% with 400 mg. The need for remedication within 6 hours was less frequent with higher doses, with 48% of participants requiring remedication after 200 mg and 42% after 400 mg. The median time to remedication was 4.7 hours for 200 mg and 5.4 hours for 400 mg. Sensitivity analyses suggested that the type of pain model and the formulation of ibuprofen could influence the results. For example, studies using dental impaction pain models and soluble ibuprofen salts showed better efficacy outcomes. Adverse events were infrequent and did not differ significantly between ibuprofen and placebo groups. In conclusion, the substantial body of high-quality evidence confirms that ibuprofen is an effective analgesic for managing postoperative pain. The NNT values for 200 mg and 400 mg doses remained consistent with the previous review, even with the inclusion of new data. Additionally, this review provides new insights into the timing and frequency of remedication.
